newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sabena sees unchanged ex-Germany cargo rate.
newsitem.headline: Sabena sees unchanged ex-Germany cargo rate.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena SA said it foresees stable ex-Germany air cargo market rates this autumn following a slump earlier this year.

Joachim Brouwer, Sabena cargo manager Germany, told Reuters in an interview: "My expectation is that up to the end of the years there will be a slight rise in volume and hopefully a stabilisation, if not a rise, in rates."
On Sabena's autumn price policy, he said: "We have a status quo in our policy. We would welcome it if the market leader increases its prices and we would follow straight away."
Brouwer said the airline's rates have stabilised since falling below 1995 levels at the start of the year.

He noted Sabena is now under less pressure to bring out spot rates as its available capacity has been reduced since last year by flight cancellations and moves from mixed to passenger-configuration aircraft.
This affects freight capacity to North America and South-East Asia, in particular, he pointed out.
Swissair owns 49.5 percent of Sabena with the remainder held by the Belgian state.
